problems.question: What is the number of stars: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐?
problems.rationale: When we count each star one at a time, we say one, two, three, four, five. The last number counted tells us the total amount. Therefore, there are 5 stars.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to point to each star sticker with their finger as they count aloud to reinforce one-to-one correspondence.
successCriteria: Count a collection of up to 5 objects with one-to-one correspondence.
Recognize and select the numeral that matches the counted quantity.
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.question: What helps a plant grow big and strong?
problems.rationale: Plants need sunshine and water to make food and grow healthy. Candy and toys cannot help living plants grow. Giving a plant sunlight keeps its leaves green and strong!
problems.teachingNote: Remind students that while animals and humans eat food, plants need natural sunlight and water to stay alive.
successCriteria: Identify sunlight as a basic need for plants to grow.
problems.subject: SCIENCE

problems.question: Which farm animal says moo?
problems.rationale: A cow makes a loud moo sound on the farm. Pigs make an oink sound, and ducks make a quack sound. That means the cow is the animal that says moo!
problems.teachingNote: Have students practice imitating different animal sounds aloud to build strong auditory connections to farm animals.
successCriteria: Identify the sound made by a cow
Distinguish between common farm animal sounds
